title: Ole Miss downplays collective head’s claim that FBI swept for ‘bugs’ after Lane Kiffin’s exit
content:
Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said “there was no hiring process” to bring in the FBI to sweep the Manning Center — the Rebels’ football performance center — after Lane Kiffin’s departure to LSU.

Golding was asked about the scenario at his weekly press conference on Monday after comments over the weekend from Walker Jones, the executive director of the Grove Collective, Ole Miss’ third-party NIL collective, in an appearance on the Assorted Crackers podcast: “We actually had the FBI come through and walk the building for bugs and for everything. We knew what was in Baton Rouge and how they operated. I remember getting on my knees and looking underneath the desk checking for some sort of bug in my office. Somebody was like, ‘What are you doing?’ I’m like, ‘Trust me, you don’t know this guy like I do.’”

Golding told reporters that Ole Miss has a current player whose father works for the FBI and lives in town. After Kiffin’s departure, Golding led the Rebels to a Sugar Bowl win over Georgia and an appearance in the College Football Playoff semifinals. Golding, who was Alabama’s defensive coordinator during three different Playoff seasons, said that “obviously, you’re going to up security” during high-stakes postseason runs.

Naturally, there were concerns about Kiffin raiding the roster when it became apparent that he was leaving Ole Miss. But only five Rebels followed Kiffin to LSU. That group was headlined by edge rusher Pricewill Umanmielen, linebacker TJ Dottery and now tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who spent the last few months with the Cleveland Browns before heading to Baton Rouge.

Ole Miss was able to keep a good chunk of its roster, including star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who ranked No. 1 in The Athletic’s 2026 College Quarterback Tiers, and All-American running back Kewan Lacy. The Rebels are ranked ninth in the preseason AP Top 25 because of their returning talent and the transfer portal additions they’ve made this offseason.

“We battled and we were able to hold on to a majority of our roster,” Jones said during the podcast interview. “Our athletic director (Keith Carter) and our chancellor (Glenn Boyce) did a great job hiring Pete. He was the logical hire. He was the locker room hire. That’s what the players wanted. We knew we had a chance to retain a ton of talent and be a top-10 team coming into this year, which we are.”

Several former Ole Miss staff members who worked for the program during the Playoff run had already agreed to join Kiffin at LSU, offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. being the most notable example.

“Half the staff was going to LSU,” Jones said. “We had to have two different text threads. Two different staff meetings. We had to ask coaches to leave the room. No hallway conversations. Nothing written down. Nothing written on the greaseboards in the office because half the staff, we were going to be competing against.”

They’ll make their return to Oxford, along with Kiffin, when Ole Miss hosts No. 11 LSU on Sept. 19 in one of the most anticipated games of the season.
